Open Start and type your company name, your planning cost per km, your wanted and lowest margin, the km one truck should drive per month and the cost of an hour of waiting time in the yellow cells.
Check Trucks, Drivers, Customers and Lanes. Keep the same names and ids as in the other parts of the Trucking suite so every page finds the right phone and rate.
Each month enter the costs and the km on Cost per Km by Month. The total cost, the cost per km driven and per loaded km, the profit and the break-even revenue fill in by themselves.
Use Cost per Km by Truck and Truck Profit by Month to see which truck costs most per km and which trucks drive fewer km than their break-even.
Read Lane Profitability and Lanes to Raise or Drop every quarter: a lane with a long empty return shows its empty km cost and a plain action (keep, raise the rate, find a backhaul or drop).
Read Rate Floor by Lane before the dispatcher books: the floor rate and the target rate per km come from the real cost of each lane.
Use Customer Profitability for the rate talks, and log every request on Rate Requests with the asked rate, the start date and the answer.
Keep Cost Categories, Fixed Costs and Overhead and Driver Cost per Km current so the split between variable and fixed cost and the driver cost per km stay true.
Type a change on Price Swing Scenarios (diesel, pay, repairs, tolls, km) and read the new cost per km and the change in margin; add notes on Cost Trend Notes whenever something moves the cost.

Use the 14 calculators: cost per km, cost per loaded km, load profit, break-even rate, floor rate, fixed cost per km, break-even km, lane compare, empty km, fuel price, driver pay, truck profit, adding a truck and a rate and cost grid.

Read Costs and Profit Dashboard and Charts every month: cost per km, margin, the lanes and customers that lose money, empty km cost and break-even per truck. Rates and costs are demo numbers: check your own.
Know your profit, your cash and the next truck decision

Payables run with due and overdue flags
workshop, tyre, insurance, fuel card, driver and lender bills with the days to due and a phone ready for the payment message
every loan and lease with the months left, the balance, the interest still to pay and the next payment date
Tax instalments and fuel tax by region
business tax instalments with the reserve set aside and fuel tax filings by region and quarter, each with a due soon warning
Truck purchase plan: replace or add
twelve offers with loan, payment, interest, added fixed cost, profit after the added cost and the cash left after the deposit
Growth scenarios for one or two more trucks

The owner, dispatcher, bookkeeper and drivers with the phone used by the message links; expense claims and year-end items find the person here.
One row per month with revenue and every cost: gross profit, operating profit, margin, owner draw, net after draw, break-even revenue and the cost per km fill in by themselves.
Loads and revenue of each customer in each month; the average per load, the share of the month and the rank of the customer fill in, so a customer that grows or fades is visible.
Every cost outside fuel, driver pay and repairs: who claimed it, the receipt and the approval; the month, the monthly budget of the category and the receipt check fill in.
The twelve expense categories with a monthly budget; the last month, the last twelve months, the variance and an over or within budget check fill in from the Expenses page.
Money in and out of the bank each month: customer receipts, invoice advances and every payment; money in, money out, net cash and the closing balance against your safety cash fill in.
Type the expected receipts and payments of each week; the closing balance starts from the bank balance in Start and an under-safety-cash warning appears when it falls below your safety cash.
Every open invoice with its due date and how many days this customer usually takes; the age, the days overdue, the expected payment date and the cash really tied up fill in.
Workshop, tyre, insurance, fuel card, driver and lender bills with the due date; the days to due and an overdue or due soon check fill in, and the phone is ready for a payment message.
Each truck loan and trailer lease with the payment, the months left and the balance; the total still to pay, the interest left and the share of the debt fill in.
Each quarterly instalment with its due date, the amount and what you have set aside; the days to due, the reserve shortfall and a due soon check fill in. Demo amounts: check your own rules.
Fuel tax payments by quarter and region
The fuel tax filing of each region and quarter: the net tax (a credit shows as a minus), the due date and the status; the days to due and a due soon check fill in.
The plan for each month against what happened: planned and actual revenue and cost; the profit, the variance and an ahead or behind plan check fill in.
The invoice advances of each month with the fee and the reserve the provider holds; the cost of the advance, the fee as a share of revenue and the share of revenue advanced fill in.
Twelve offers to replace TR-05 or add a truck: price, deposit, rate and months; the payment, interest, added fixed cost, profit after cost and cash left after the deposit fill in.
What happens if you add one or two trucks and haul more loads: revenue, cost and profit per month and the loads needed to break even fill in from the load rate and cost.

Bank statement lines to match with receipts and payments: the date, the text, the amount and what it matches; the direction, the days open and a check fill in so nothing stays unmatched.
The credit limit, what was drawn and repaid each month and the rate; the interest, the room left and a safe or tight check fill in.
The eight trucks and ten trailers with the purchase price, the date and the life in years; the yearly depreciation, the age, the book value and the years left fill in.
Every document and job to finish before the year-end close with the person responsible and the due date; the days to due and an on time, late or done check fill in.

Open Start and type your company name, your safety cash (the bank balance you never want to go under), your wanted operating margin and the bank balance today in the yellow cells.
Keep the Team page with the real phones: expense claims, year-end items and the message links read them.
Each month enter revenue, km and the cost lines on Profit and Loss by Month. Gross profit, operating profit, margin, break-even revenue and the net after the owner draw fill in by themselves.
Enter the bank figures of the month on Cash Flow by Month and see the closing balance against your safety cash.
Every week move Cash Forecast 13 Weeks on: type the expected receipts and payments of each week and read the closing balance and the warning before the bank runs low.
Keep Receivables, Payables and Bank Reconciliation current: the age and days overdue, the due soon flags and the unmatched lines tell you what to do this week.
Use Expenses and Expense Budget to approve claims, collect receipts and compare each category with its budget.

Keep Truck Financing, Asset Register, Business Tax, Fuel Tax Payments and Line of Credit current so every payment date and balance is visible. Tax amounts are demo inputs: check your own rules and rates.
Compare offers on Truck Purchase Plan and Growth Scenarios before you replace TR-05 or add a truck; read the profit after the added cost and the cash left after the deposit.

Use the 14 calculators: profit and loss, break-even, cash forecast, runway, slow payer gap, factoring, owner draw, truck affordability, loan or lease, working capital, tax estimate, depreciation, budget check and a revenue and cost grid.
Read Finance and Cash Dashboard and Charts every month. The numbers are demo values for a small carrier: replace them with your own.
